dataset: National BIM mandates: regulatory status by jurisdiction
author: Ivan Shtaer

status_scale.mandatory: BIM legally/contractually required now for a defined class of (usually public) projects
status_scale.partial: required by value threshold, sector, phase-in, or by a specific public agency rather than nationwide
status_scale.voluntary: official roadmap / strategy / declaration / recommended standard, not yet binding

eu_context.title: EU Directive 2014/24/EU, Art. 22(4) — permits member states to require BIM in public procurement

note: Every entry is anchored to an official primary source (decree, law, circular, adopted standard or official government programme). Some government portals are geo-restricted or JavaScript-rendered.

jurisdictions.name: United Kingdom
jurisdictions.instrument: Level 2 BIM mandate (2016, from the 2011 Government Construction Strategy); enforced in public procurement via The Construction Playbook (UK BIM Framework / BS EN ISO 19650)
jurisdictions.authority: Cabinet Office; Infrastructure and Projects Authority (IPA)
jurisdictions.effective: Level 2 BIM mandatory for central-government projects since April 2016; UK BIM Framework required for public works on a 'comply or explain' basis
jurisdictions.summary: More than a roadmap. Collaborative (Level 2) BIM has been required on all centrally-procured central-government projects since April 2016, and the Construction Playbook obliges central departments and their arm's-length bodies — on a 'comply or explain' basis — to apply the UK BIM Framework (BS EN ISO 19650) in how public works are procured and delivered; the IPA's Transforming Infrastructure Performance roadmap carries it forward.
jurisdictions.ifc_standards: BS EN ISO 16739 (IFC schema); ISO 19650 process; IFC not mandated for exchange
jurisdictions.qualification_scheme: Digital Engineering Technician occupational standard (ST0266); RICS / BSI ISO 19650 individual certification

jurisdictions.name: Czech Republic
jurisdictions.instrument: Act No. 330/2025 Sb. — Zákon o BIM (Act on management of information about construction and the built environment)

The Act takes effect on 1 January 2027 (built-environment model from 2030; certain information containers from 2032), replacing the earlier voluntary concept.

jurisdictions.name: United States
jurisdictions.instrument: GSA agency requirement (model-based design + IFC); binding state mandates — WI, TX, OH, GA, MA
jurisdictions.authority: U.S. General Services Administration (GSA); state facilities agencies; NIBS (standard)
jurisdictions.effective: GSA requires native + IFC deliverables; states require BIM for state-funded buildings above value thresholds
jurisdictions.summary: No federal BIM law. Much US activity is program and guidance — the GSA BIM Guides and the consensus National BIM Standard-US (NBIMS-US, NIBS). Binding requirements exist at two levels: the GSA requires model-based design with native + IFC deliverables on its federal projects, and five states mandate BIM for their own state-funded buildings — Wisconsin (first, 2009; now > $15M new / > $3M tenant-improvement), Texas (TFC), Ohio (OFCC), Georgia (GSFIC) and Massachusetts (DCAMM, ≥ $1M). Others publish BIM guidelines only (e.g. New York, Tennessee, Florida), and several DOTs (TxDOT, Caltrans, Iowa) mandate digital delivery for transport infrastructure; most states have no requirement.
jurisdictions.ifc_standards: IFC (ISO 16739) via NBIMS-US; GSA & AASHTO require IFC; no single national adoption
jurisdictions.qualification_scheme: AGC CM-BIM certificate; buildingSMART USA (BIMForum)

jurisdictions.name: Switzerland
jurisdictions.instrument: Federal building bodies (KBOB) BIM requirements; armasuisse & SBB adopt BIM from 2025; federal EMBAG 'open by default' law (in force 2024)
jurisdictions.authority: KBOB; armasuisse Immobilien; SBB (federal railways); Confederation (EMBAG)
jurisdictions.effective: Major federal projects (armasuisse Immobilien) and SBB phase BIM in from 2025; EMBAG in force 1 Jan 2024
jurisdictions.summary: No BIM-specific national mandate and no single BIM regulator. The federal building and property bodies — coordinated via KBOB (armasuisse Immobilien, BBL, ETH-Rat, ASTRA) — apply BIM on major federal projects from 2025, and the federal railway SBB is phasing BIM in from 2025 (agency/owner-level requirements). Underpinning this, the federal EMBAG law (in force 1 Jan 2024) sets an 'open by default' principle for authorities — open-source software (Art. 9) and open government data (Art. 10) — which reinforces an open-standards / openBIM (IFC) approach across federal bodies, though EMBAG does not itself name BIM.
jurisdictions.ifc_standards: SN EN ISO 16739 (IFC); SIA 2051; KBOB; federal 'open by default' law (EMBAG, 2024)
jurisdictions.qualification_scheme: buildingSMART Switzerland (Bauen digital Schweiz) certification
